What's new in v43 — tap to read
  • Entry Tracker — track your real fills (v43) — you still place every trade yourself in Kalshi; the app now records and tracks the fill you actually got. Tap "I bought this — lock entry" on the Trade Screen or the Best Decision card, confirm your real entry price and contract count (prefilled from the live Kalshi ask and the app's sizing math — edit either to match your fill), and an Entry Tracker card appears on Targets under Trade Watch: your coin, side and window, entry price, contracts and stake, the live Kalshi price for your side, your live value and live P&L after both taker fees, and your ladder lines — the 2× lock (sell half to recover your stake plus the entry fee) and the 3× step (sell a quarter to lock cash profit), each marked REACHED or how many cents away it is. The 2× and 3× crossings chime and buzz once each, like the Trade Watch ladder. A slim ACTIVE ENTRY strip rides the front screen while a fill is open. Bought out early? Tap "I exited early", type your exit price, and the fill settles as an EXIT with the realized P&L after both fees. Left it to the close? It grades itself at the window close — win, loss, or a push on an exact tie — with the P&L after the entry fee. One entry at a time; a wrong tap can be voided and records nothing.
  • Your real fills drive your discipline now — Your locked real fills now drive the cooldown and the late-session 1-loss stop for their window (real beats paper, never double-counted). When a window has both a settled real fill and a paper round call, the real result is the one that counts toward the 2-loss cooldown and the late-session stop; when a window has only the paper call, everything works exactly as before. Win Rate gains a YOUR REAL FILLS record — wins, losses, pushes and early exits, your net P&L after fees, your hit rate, and your late-session fills split out — labeled as recorded by you, and kept separate from the paper Round Record and the relay's real Kalshi record, always.
  • Late-session 20% stake is real (v42) — Late session stake is now your real rule: rounds you lock between 11 PM and midnight stake 20% of the book; the rest of the day stays 10%. The Late Session panel now shows the rule as ACTIVE in the window instead of display only, and rounds booked at 20% are marked "late-session 20% stake" in the Round Record, with their own line on Win Rate. Every guard is unchanged — stopped, on a break, vault-halted or in cooldown, nothing books at any size.
  • Alerts you can hear and feel (v41) — Trade Watch warnings, principal-recovery alerts, ladder step 2 and flip alerts now play a short chime and buzz your phone, each with its own sound so you can tell them apart. The sounds are made inside the app — no audio files. Turn sound or vibration on or off any time in Settings & Safety → Alerts.
  • Keep your screen awake (v41) — a new option in the same Alerts card: while it's on, the app asks your phone to keep the screen awake while the app is open, and a small WAKE ON tag shows in the hero while it's actually holding. If your phone says no, nothing breaks — the tag just stays hidden. It still doesn't make the app run while it's closed.
  • Ladder step 2 at 3× (v41) — Trade Watch's ladder gains its second step: after the 2× principal-recovery alert, the first time your side's Kalshi price reaches 3× your entry you get a one-time alert — "LADDER STEP 2 — selling another quarter of the original position here locks in cash profit — the last quarter rides to settlement" — with the after-fee dollars for that quarter sale, worked out with the same fee helper as everything else, and logged with your watched trades. Like step 1, it only ever fires off a Kalshi price that actually loaded — never off the Coinbase line.
  • Final-minute settlement tracker (v41) — in the last 60 seconds of a round, the Trade Screen (and the board's BEST BET row) starts averaging the app's own price samples live: "Settlement avg so far (app samples): $X · 47/60s locked in · holding ABOVE the line by $Y". When that average sits within 0.03% of the line it flags a COIN-FLIP ZONE in amber. Kalshi settles on the 60-second average of its own index — this tracker uses the app's Coinbase samples, an estimate, not the official index, and it says so right on the tracker.
  • Spread check on the board (v41) — Kalshi's feed carries bid prices as well as asks, so every board row now shows each side's spread (ask − bid, in cents). And a spread over 3¢ on the side the app would play caps Best Decision at DON'T PLACE with the number in the reason — "spread 5¢ — over the 3¢ quality cap". A wide spread is a bad fill waiting to happen; the app now says no for you.
  • Late Session is in (v40) — your own 11 PM–12 AM ET discipline, as a display + paper layer in the app. The window is 11:00 PM to midnight Eastern, BTC and ETH only. A new Late Session card sits on Targets right under the Session card: it shows whether the session is coming up, live (with the round count, 4 max), stopped, on a break, or at target — plus your hour-start balance against your current tracked Kalshi balance. The app still places nothing; every stake stays your tap in Kalshi.
  • 1-loss stop — one round call that settles as a loss inside the 11 PM hour ends your day in the app: Best Decision caps at DON'T PLACE with the reason "late session — 1-loss stop hit; done for the day", and God Mode tickets and Kalshi Lab combos can't lock. It is stricter than the v39 2-loss cooldown and speaks first after a vault halt.
  • 3-day break — if the app sees a new day after a late session and your tracked balance is under the balance you started that hour with, a 3-day break latches: Best Decision caps at DON'T PLACE — "3-day break — late session ended under its $X start; back <date>" — the panel shows BREAK with the return date, and the hero carries a red BREAK pill. The break is checked once for that session, never re-latched on later days.
  • $100 target + Road to $100 — when your tracked balance reaches $100 the state latches TARGET REACHED (green pill on the hero, state line on the panel) — a plain fact, nothing more claimed. The panel's Road to $100 block does the thread's math from your current balance: rounds needed if every round wins at +20%, and net wins needed at 20% risk with +40% gains (+8% a net win) — from $14.84 that's 11 rounds and 25 net wins — captioned as math only: the all-wins line assumes zero losses, and real paths take longer.
  • Session candidate, with your math shown — while the hour is live, the panel reads BTC and ETH off the real Kalshi board (the YES ask — never the Coinbase fallback; if Kalshi hasn't loaded it says so, and volume shows only when the Kalshi feed actually carries it). The coin with a YES ask at 55¢ or more — the higher volume when both qualify and volume is known — is marked SESSION CANDIDATE, with your late-session rule written out as display only: limit 56¢ · stake 20% of your tracked balance = the dollar stake → the contracts it buys · the taker fee from the same shared fee helper · the breakeven win rate. If neither coin qualifies, the panel says "No session candidate — your rules say sit out this round." The 20% figure is shown for the late session only — the virtual paper book's sizing is unchanged.
  • Binance cross-check on the board — every Market Board row gains a small third line when Binance's public price loads: "Binance $X (±N bps vs Coinbase)", refreshed on the board's existing cadence. It is labeled cross-check only in the board header, it hides silently whenever Binance doesn't answer, and it never feeds a decision, a prediction or a grade.
  • Session discipline is in (v39) — four guards that protect a good session from a bad hour: a profit vault with a session floor, a 2-loss cooldown, a velocity check on every play, and a principal-recovery alert on watched trades. All of it runs off numbers the app already tracks — your Kalshi balance (typed by you or synced by the read-only relay) and the app's own round record. Nothing new is invented, and the app still places nothing.
  • The Profit Vault — each day (Eastern) the session anchors at your tracked Kalshi balance: the vault floor starts at 70% of where you started. As your balance climbs to a new peak, the floor ratchets up to lock in half the gain — start $14.84, peak $20.00, and the floor becomes $17.42. If your balance touches the floor, the session halts: VAULT HALT — Best Decision stops calling plays ("vault halt — balance $X hit the session floor $Y; session locked"), God Mode tickets and Kalshi Lab combos can't lock, and round calls stop locking too. The halt stays latched until you tap "Start new session" on the Session card (Targets, under the Round Record) or a new day begins. The hero shows one compact line — "Vault floor $X · peak $Y" — plus a red VAULT HALT pill while you're halted.
  • Predictions keep measuring through a halt — a vault halt or a cooldown stops plays and locks, but predictions keep locking and grading exactly as before. The app never stops measuring itself just because it stopped calling plays.
  • 2-loss cooldown — two straight losing round calls and the app sits out: for 15 minutes Best Decision caps at DON'T PLACE ("cooldown — 2 straight losses, back at 2:35 PM ET"), tickets and combos can't lock, and round calls don't lock. A win resets the count; when the 15 minutes run out the count resets too. The hero shows an amber COOLDOWN pill while it runs, and Win Rate's new Session Recap counts how many cooldowns fired today.
  • Velocity confirmation on plays — a PLACE now also needs the coin actually moving your way: the 1-minute spot velocity (from the price samples the app already keeps) must be at least +0.05% for an UP play or −0.05% for a DOWN play. Flat chop no longer gets a play: the reason says it in numbers — "1m velocity +0.01% — under the +0.05% confirmation for UP" — and when there aren't 45 seconds of samples yet it says "1m velocity not confirmed yet — only Xs of samples" instead of guessing. A passing check shows in the reason: "1m velocity +0.07% ✓". God Mode legs get the same per-leg check, with the failing reason shown on the closest candidate.
  • Principal-recovery alerts — arm a Trade Watch and, the first time your side's real Kalshi price reaches twice your entry, you get a one-time alert: "PRINCIPAL RECOVERY — BTC Yes at 89¢ is 2× your 44¢ entry: selling half here returns $A of your $B stake after fees — the rest rides free." The dollars come from your watch's stake and the same fee helper as everything else, and it's logged with your watched trades. It only ever fires off a Kalshi price that actually loaded — never off the Coinbase line.
  • Maker-first fee note — next to the taker fee on the Best Decision line and the Trade Screen: "Maker-first: a limit at ask −1¢ pays $0 fee (vs $X taker)" — the taker figure is the same shared fee helper at the displayed price and size. Display only; how you place stays your call in Kalshi.
  • Session card + Session Recap — Targets gains a compact Session card by the Round Record: start / peak / current balance, the vault floor, session P&L (labeled "from your tracked Kalshi balance"), the state line (ACTIVE / VAULT HALT / COOLDOWN until …) and the two-tap "Start new session" reset. Win Rate gains a Session Recap: today's start, peak, current and floor, whether the floor was hit, rounds won–lost today, cooldowns triggered today, and yesterday's one-liner when there is one.
  • Round-state guards (v38) — every Superbrain read now runs under one shared round state, worked out from the window clock and whether the real Kalshi strike has loaded: STRIKE LOCKING (the first 30 seconds of a window, or the strike hasn't loaded yet — the Coinbase fallback line never counts as a locked strike), LIVE, and SETTLEMENT ZONE (the final 75 seconds — Kalshi settles on a 60-second average of its index, so late moves count for less and the book thins out). The state is visible at a glance: a chip in the Market Board header shows it with its countdown.
  • Nothing locks at the edges of a round — while the strike is locking, Best Decision says NO DECISION and says why in numbers ("strike still locking — 12s into the window", or "Kalshi strike not loaded yet"); in the settlement zone a PLACE is capped at DON'T PLACE — "settlement zone — 41s left, Kalshi settles on a 60-second average; no new entries" — while leans still show. Predictions never lock in either state (the late fallback lock never lands inside the final 75 seconds), entry signals and entry early warnings don't fire, Kalshi Lab combos and God Mode tickets can't lock, and an armed Trade Watch warns you once — "settlement zone — exit window closing" — and shows "waiting for strike lock" in a fresh window until the strike lands. STRIKE CROSS and REGIME CHANGE still record, tagged with the round state.
  • Kalshi's real taker fee is in the math now — one shared helper runs Kalshi's published taker schedule (fee = ceil(0.07 × contracts × price × (1 − price) × 100) / 100, price in dollars; maker / resting-limit fills are $0 on standard 15-min series). When a PLACE verdict shows a price cap, the card adds the fee at that price for your Trade Watch size (or $1) and the breakeven after fees — "at 65¢, taker fee ≈ $0.03 on $1 — breakeven 67.0% after fees".
  • EV is shown after fees — board rows, the Trade Screen, predictions and Kalshi Lab show "EV after fees" next to the gross figure whenever the fee changes it. The God Mode gate now tests the after-fee EV: a leg that is only positive before fees no longer passes. Combo and God Mode tickets show payout and joint EV after estimated per-leg taker fees, labeled "after estimated taker fees — limit fills are $0".
  • The paper book pays the modeled fee too — newly settled round calls deduct a modeled taker entry fee at the 55¢ entry assumption, for the contracts the stake buys, labeled "fee −$0.0X modeled" on the round — so the virtual record stays honest. Rounds settled before v38 are not re-graded.
  • Settlement, labeled straight — Win Rate and the Targets record now carry the line where results settle: "Kalshi settles on a 60-second average of its index — the app grades on the Coinbase close, a proxy." No grading changed — ties are still pushes (v33).
  • Front-screen functional pass (v37) — every control on the front screen was traced to the code behind it and fixed where the tap didn't do what the control says it does. The fixes below are in the code, not just the labels.
  • BEST AVAILABLE works in every state now — the strip was a button that did nothing whenever it said "wait" or "syncing" (its most common states). Now: a live best bet still opens that coin's Trade Screen, a forming setup still opens Targets, the "nothing available" state opens Targets (where the full read behind the wait lives), and the "syncing" state re-runs Refresh. Its label updates to say what the tap will do.
  • Auto-Run is Superbrain-only in the code, not just the card — the front switch's lanes list dropped EdgeBoard in v31, but pressing RUN still quietly started EdgeBoard's bot timer and kept it alive after you left EdgeBoard. That coupling is removed: RUN starts only the Superbrain lanes it lists, EdgeBoard's timer now exists only while EdgeBoard is open, and its bot auto-build runs on its own cadence while EdgeBoard is open — EdgeBoard governs itself, exactly like its scans. EdgeBoard's manual "Run the bot" button is untouched.
  • Refresh is hardened and honest — one failing background render can no longer take the whole Refresh down with it (each piece is guarded on its own now), the hero chip flips to SYNCING… the moment you tap, the front Objectives summary re-renders with everything else, and the toast says "re-syncing" instead of claiming "re-synced" before the reads land.
  • The front screen updates as one screen — the BEST AVAILABLE strip and the Signals panel now re-render on the same 3-second front tick as Best Decision and the Market Board, instead of only when the Targets tab ticked — the strip can no longer sit stale next to a fresh board.
  • Front cards work from the keyboard too — Best Decision, the Trade Watch line, the Kalshi balance and every section-menu item are focusable and answer Enter/Space, the same as a tap. They were tap-only divs before.
  • The $10 Desk is now a 7-agent desk — a REVIEWER joined the pipeline: Scout → Filter → Analyst → Risk → Executor → Reviewer → Logger. Every paper open the Executor prepares is checked by the Reviewer first — the price read must be fresh (15 seconds or less), the Analyst scorecard complete, the risk limits intact (no day halt, open-count and sizing caps), no duplicate open on the same coin, and the live price still within 10% of the prepared entry. Approve and it opens; veto and it never opens — the veto reason, in numbers, is written to the desk log and counted on the desk screen. Every desk rule you set is unchanged.
  • The desk screen is a live dashboard now — swipable agent cards at the top show what each of the seven agents did most recently (or “standing by”), a big equity number carries today's session P&L, the equity line is drawn only from real recorded points (a point lands when a trade opens or closes and when you open the desk screen — under 2 points it says so instead of drawing a curve), session stats show today's (ET) closed fills, win rate, realized P&L and vetoes next to the all-time line, an Activity feed lists the latest desk events with their times, and a “Session reconciled” line appears when the book is flat with fills booked today.
  • Superbrain screens update while you look at them — Targets, Win Rate, the $10 Desk, the Betting Desk (the God Mode Parlay Builder's ticket included) and Kalshi Lab now refresh live on the app's own tick, about every 5 seconds per screen — no more reopening a tab to see new numbers. Targets keeps its faster cadence, your scroll spot is kept, and a screen never redraws while you're typing in one of its boxes. EdgeBoard is untouched — it keeps its own update path, exactly as the separation requires.
  • The $1 Parlay Bot is now the God Mode Parlay Builder — in the Betting Desk. It builds parlays only from Kalshi 15-minute legs that clear the God Mode gate — nothing else gets on a ticket, and when nothing clears it, it says so plainly instead of forcing a build.
  • The gate, in plain numbers — a leg qualifies only when ALL four hold: the model's calibrated confidence is 60% or more, the value against the live Kalshi ask is positive, the ask actually loaded (never the Coinbase fallback line), and the ask is 85¢ or less. Every leg in the current window shows its gate check in the builder — pass, or the one reason it failed, in numbers.
  • Real joint math, honest payout — tickets are same-window combos of 2–4 passing legs, ranked by the correlation-adjusted joint chance (the same math as Kalshi Lab combos, never shown above 97%), with the independence figure shown alongside, labeled. The top ticket shows its legs, the combined price, what your stake pays — the stake field starts at $1, change it and the payout updates — and the expected killer: the weakest leg, named plainly. When the top ticket runs 3–4 legs, the best 2-leg ticket shows separately, labeled safer — fewer legs.
  • Slip out, paper-logged, graded — Copy slip makes a clean text slip (legs, sides, prices, joint chance, payout) to paste into Kalshi or Gambly — the app places nothing. Lock ticket (paper) keeps the ticket on this phone, and it settles with the same window-close grading as predictions and combos: every leg right wins, any leg wrong loses, and a leg that finishes exactly on its line pushes the whole ticket only when every other leg won. The record shows in the builder and as GOD MODE PARLAYS on the Win Rate screen. The Auto-Run lane is renamed too — "Parlay Bot rebuild" is now "God Mode Parlay rebuild": while Auto-Run is on, the builder refreshes its top ticket as new windows open.
  • Round calls got their lock guard, and the last stale feed lines are cleaned up — a round call now never locks inside the final 3:00 of a window (the same no-entry line the decision engine already used): a setup that only completes after 3:00 left makes no call at all instead of a late, low-quality lock. When a call does lock and Kalshi has loaded, the round now records the real Kalshi ask for the called side at that moment — shown on the round as "Kalshi ask at lock NN¢", never estimated. The Auto-Run lane list no longer says the desk is waiting on the live feed, and the old Feed uptime objective is retired — the feed is gone, so nothing is scored against keeping it connected. And the "Open in Phantom" buttons are gone: they were built from the app's own address, so instead the wallet card now tells you plainly how to open the app inside Phantom or Solflare's own browser and connect there.
  • The live coin feed is removed — for real this time — you ordered pump.fun out of the app earlier, and the screens went in v20, but the live feed underneath was still connecting. Now it's deleted from the app itself: no WebSocket to the old feed host, no new-coin subscription, no token-trade subscriptions, and Connection Check no longer reaches out to that host. Your follow list was already staying on this phone (since v20) and still does.
  • What that changes on the $10 Desk — SCOUT no longer receives new pairs as they launch, and the Executor's automatic dip-buys — which keyed off the stream — stay off. Everything else about the desk is untouched: its records, balance, Decision Log and Morning Brief stay, candidates can still be added by hand, and the desk still re-checks them every 20 seconds while the app is open. The feed status line and the desk's SCOUT stage say "removed" plainly instead of pretending to reconnect.
  • Real pump.fun trades are removed too — the removal is complete now: the trade builder that used to assemble real buys and sells is deleted, along with every "Buy with Real SOL" / "Sell (Real)" button and the real-trade confirm card. Nothing in this app can build, sign or send a real pump.fun trade anymore — practice and paper trades are untouched. What remains is only links out: a coin or profile link opens pump.fun in your browser when you tap it, and nothing is sent anywhere. Targets, Best Decision, Signals, Kalshi Lab, EdgeBoard, the relay and every record on both sides work exactly as before.
  • The hit-rate fix pack is in — an inspection of the prediction model found real drag costing points, and all six fixes are now live. Straight line first: no fix makes a market read 100% — prices move and some windows are coin flips. What changed is the app no longer manufactures false confidence or grades itself unfairly.
  • Pace is measured over ~45 seconds now, and the projection is damped — the model used to stretch the last ~4 seconds of motion across the whole 15 minutes, so a tiny early wiggle could read as 95% confidence. Pace now comes from a ~45-second window, and the projected finish assumes the pace fades (a 60-second decay) instead of running flat-out to the close. Momentum and the early warnings read the same steadier pace.
  • Confidence is capped until the record earns more — 75% while fewer than 30 predictions have settled, 85% until 100 have, and 95% only when the 80%+ band itself has 20+ settled calls that actually hit 80%+. A short pace read (under 30 seconds of motion) also pulls confidence toward a coin flip.
  • The accuracy table now feeds back — Win Rate → Predictions has always shown how often each confidence band was really right; the model now uses it. A new prediction's confidence is pulled toward what its band actually earned, once that band has 10+ settled calls — if "80%" calls have really been hitting 60%, the app stops saying 80%.
  • Hit rates are split by lock type, with counts — Predictions no longer blends its two kinds of lock into one number: PLACE locks (locked when the decision said PLACE) and late locks (locked at 3:00 left when no PLACE fired) each show their own hit rate with their win/loss counts, next to the overall rate.
  • Exact ties are pushes now — a prediction that finishes exactly on the line is graded a push: neither a win nor a loss, and out of the hit rate — the same way the Round Record already treats its ties. Predictions settled before this update keep the result they were given. And when a prediction's line was Kalshi's strike, its settled note now says plainly that it was graded on the Coinbase close, a proxy for Kalshi's own settlement index.
  • The self-learner is slower — the round-call learner used to tighten a coin's rules after a single loss, which mostly made it call less, not read better. Now the same kind of miss has to happen twice in a row on a coin before any rule moves (a win in between resets the count). The first miss is still named in plain words and logged — it just doesn't move a threshold by itself.
  • Best Decision and Signals are Superbrain's own — they run off the Kalshi board and spot reads only, nothing to do with EdgeBoard. The Best Decision call, the BEST AVAILABLE strip and every signal and early warning are worked out purely from Superbrain's own reads — Coinbase spot and candles, the Kalshi 15-minute board strips and the Targets state. No EdgeBoard data, scan, gate value or timing feeds them, holds them up or labels them.
  • They run even if EdgeBoard was never opened — Best Decision and Signals render and update on Superbrain's own read cycle with EdgeBoard untouched, empty or never visited. You'll see it labeled right on the front screen: a line under the Best Decision card — "Superbrain's own read — not tied to EdgeBoard" — and the same note at the top of the Signals panel.
  • The front screen no longer runs EdgeBoard — Auto-Run is Superbrain-only now: the master switch runs the $10 Desk pipeline, the Targets reads and the God Mode Parlay rebuild, and that's it. The EdgeBoard scans lane is gone from the switch and its Lanes list — nothing on the front screen drives, gates or waits on EdgeBoard anymore.
  • EdgeBoard scans on its own, inside its own area — while EdgeBoard is open it auto-scans on its own cadence (the 30s / 60s / 120s you set in Rules & Config), no matter what the front screen's Auto-Run switch says. It has its own on/off now — "Auto-scan while EdgeBoard is open" in Rules & Config, on by default. Turn it off and the automatic scans stop; "Scan lines now" still works by hand any time.
  • The EdgeBoard door stays — the Betting row and the area switch on the front screen are just ways in, and they work exactly as before. Nothing was deleted: every EdgeBoard record (paper bets, parlays, alerts, learning) and every Superbrain record is untouched, and the gate, the Lab, the relay and the $10 Desk all behave exactly as they did.
  • Kalshi Lab — the app now learns Kalshi's habits — a new screen under 15-Min Trading. The app can't read Kalshi's private code, so it learns their patterns from real windows it watches itself: where Kalshi sets its strike compared with the exchange open, and how Kalshi prices a contract compared with what the app's own model thinks it's worth at the same distance and time. Every learned number shows how many windows it came from, and under 30 samples it says "still learning — small sample" right on the figure.
  • Strike bias, per coin — Kalshi Lab's first table averages the gap between Kalshi's strike and the Coinbase open for BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP ("Kalshi's strike has sat ~$38 ABOVE the Coinbase open on BTC across 42 windows"). A sample is recorded only at a prediction lock and only when a real Kalshi strike actually loaded — never from the Coinbase fallback line, and never guessed.
  • Pricing calibration — the second table lines up what Kalshi charged for the model's side against what the model thought it was worth, band by band (how far spot sat from the strike, measured against each coin's own distance line). That gap is the app's empirical picture of Kalshi's pricing habits — where their price runs rich or cheap against the model.
  • Paper market combos, with honest joint chances — when 2 or more coins read 60%+ in the same window, Kalshi Lab builds combo candidates and shows the joint chance two ways: the raw number (if coins moved independently) and an adjusted number that accounts for the coins moving together, worked out from the app's own settled prediction history. No combo chance is ever shown above 97%, and nothing is called a sure thing. Lock a combo and it's kept as a paper record, graded when the window settles — a combo wins only if every leg wins. Its record and calibration line also live on the Win Rate screen under Predictions. Combos are paper records for grading — you place legs yourself in Kalshi if you play them.
  • EdgeBoard God Mode — a GOD MODE panel now sits at the top of EdgeBoard: how many plays pass the gate right now, and the single best one shown big — matchup, side, book and price, true chance and EV. Tap it and you land in Edges filtered to just the passers. When nothing passes it says so plainly — the gate is never relaxed to fill the panel.
  • More sports — EdgeBoard now scans WNBA and women's college basketball with the same predictor edge math, plus MLS, the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1 and the Champions League as lines-only sports (their free feed carries real book lines but no predictor, so they get lines and no edge math — labeled on the card). UFC/MMA was checked and left out: its free feed carries no odds at all.
  • Lines and Props, separated by sport — Lines is grouped into per-sport sections with sport chips, game counts and per-sport scan times. Props has its own screen beside Lines, grouped by sport the same way, showing real player-prop markets from Kalshi's public feed — prices only, labeled on every card, because no verified true-chance source exists for them: no EV, no gate badge, nothing invented.
  • Rules & Config — the old Rules & Learning screen is now Rules & Config: sport on/off toggles, scan cadence (30s / 60s / 120s), your Edges sort, a per-sport scan-status block, and a data panel with a clear-scan-data button that never touches paper bets, parlays, alerts or learning. The gate stays locked and read-only: EV ≥ +5% · true chance ≥ 55% · no verify flags.
  • Popups stay in their own area — a Superbrain flip popup no longer covers EdgeBoard: while you're in EdgeBoard it queues (watch for the dot on the Superbrain switch) and shows when you switch back. EdgeBoard alerts likewise wait for EdgeBoard. Nothing is dropped — display is only deferred.
  • Decision reasons now show the actual numbers — a DON'T PLACE explains itself: "distance $3.39 of $5 needed — not built yet" instead of a bare "no setup yet", the real Kalshi ask against the zone ("Yes ask 82¢ — above the 75¢ cap", "Yes ask 41¢ — below the 50¢ floor"), the leading price on a round that's already decided, and the real time left when it's too late in the window. The same numbered reason shows on the Trade Screen verdict, the front Best Decision card, and the BEST AVAILABLE strip's wait line.
  • Same 10 rules, same calls — clearer reasons — nothing about when the app says PLACE or DON'T PLACE changed; only the explanation gained the measured values behind it. And when a price hasn't loaded, the reason still says so plainly — "Kalshi prices not loaded — can't check the entry price" — instead of guessing a number.
  • Your real Kalshi balance can now sync itself — connect the read-only relay in Settings & Safety (your relay URL and token, stored only in this browser) and the hero balance updates from your real Kalshi balance on its own — on open, on Refresh, and whenever you tap Sync. Your practice book follows it, logged as an adjustment labeled "synced from Kalshi relay" — never a win or a loss, and your win rate never moves. If the relay can't be reached, the app keeps your last value and says so.
  • Your real Kalshi record is on the Win Rate screen — a new REAL KALSHI RECORD section at the very top shows your settled wins and losses, your exact net down to the cent, and your recent settlements and fills, read straight from the relay. It stays separate from the app's paper records below it — real and paper never mix.
  • The app still can't trade, and it holds no key — the relay is read-only: the app can look, never trade. Your Kalshi API key lives in your relay, never in this app — there is no key field anywhere in it. Disconnect in Settings clears the relay from this browser any time.
  • The front screen is now built around the Kalshi board — Best Decision up top, then a new BEST AVAILABLE strip, then the Market Board itself. Trade-reading stays on the Trade Screen in its tab; the front screen's one job is the board with the best available play highlighted.
  • BEST AVAILABLE — the single best play, big and tappable — right under Best Decision, one card shows the best play available right now: the coin, UP or DOWN (with the Yes/No), the price cap ("pay 65¢ or less"), the prediction confidence, the value per contract when Kalshi priced it, and the time left in the window. Tap it and you're on the Trade Screen for that coin. When nothing qualifies as a play but a setup is forming, the strip shows that instead — "FORMING — BTC building UP · $95 of $150 · not a call yet" — and when there's truly nothing, it just says wait, plain. It only ever shows a play the app's own decision engine actually produced.
  • Board rows now carry the full Kalshi board — when Kalshi loads for a coin, its row shows Kalshi's Yes bid/ask and No bid/ask in cents on their own line, next to the spot, the line, the distance, the time left and the prediction marker. When Kalshi blocks this phone, the row keeps its "Coinbase line — Kalshi blocked" label and shows "Kalshi prices —" — a Kalshi price is never substituted or invented.
  • Your practice book now follows your Kalshi balance — saving your Kalshi balance in the hero also sets the Targets virtual book to the same amount, logged as an adjustment labeled "synced to your Kalshi balance" — never a win or a loss, and your win rate and round stats never move. The "Match my Kalshi balance" button stays on the Round Record card for one-off syncs.
  • The app now warns you while a setup is forming — new EARLY WARNINGS, before the full signal fires. When a coin's move is 60% built and holding its side, you get "EARLY WARNING — BTC building UP: $95 of the $150 needed · not a call yet" as an advance heads-up.
  • Cross-coming warnings too — when spot sits close to the line and is moving fast enough to reach it within about a minute: "EARLY WARNING — ETH may cross DOWN within ~1 min at this pace". If the cross really happens, the normal STRIKE CROSS signal still fires.
  • They show on the front screen and in Signals — a slim line right under Best Decision while a warning is active (tap it to jump to Targets), and in the Signals panel with an EARLY tag. Visual only — no sound, no alarm banner: a heads-up, not a call. The full signals still fire at exactly their normal thresholds, unchanged.
  • The app now predicts every window — each coin gets a prediction with a confidence: the side it expects to win (UP or DOWN), the projected finish, and a % from this window's own volatility. It shows on the Trade Screen under the decision, on the front card's EXPECT line, and as a small ▲/▼ marker on every board row. No fresh read, no prediction — it never projects from stale prices.
  • Every prediction is checked against Kalshi's price — the app works out the value per contract (its confidence vs the ask). A PLACE whose price kills the value says so in plain words. When Kalshi is blocked, the value is honestly "unknown" — never guessed.
  • The BEST BET is now the best value — the board ranks PLACE coins by that value first; coins without a loaded Kalshi price rank below priced ones, and with no prices at all it falls back to the strongest-distance ranking.
  • And it grades itself in the open — one prediction locks per coin per window (the first PLACE, or at 3:00 left), never changes once set, and settles against the real close. Win Rate → Predictions shows the true hit rate, per coin and by confidence band — when it said 70–79%, how often it was actually right.
  • Best-experience pass — a cleaner front screen: nothing hides behind the bottom bar anymore, the first read lands faster (syncing states show right away instead of blank space), and the BEST DECISION stays pinned in view on the Trade Screen while the rest of the tab scrolls.
  • Your Kalshi balance is in the hero now — it shows the $15.52 from your screenshot until you tap it and type the balance Kalshi shows you. On the Round Record card, one tap on "Match my Kalshi balance" lines the virtual book up with it, logged as an adjustment — never a win or a loss.
  • The hero chip tells the truth about sync — SYNCED with the time, SYNCING…, or KALSHI BLOCKED — COINBASE LINE. Refresh re-syncs the board. The Auto-Run card is slimmer: one line up front, the full details inside Lanes.
  • The Paper Bot now has a tracker line on the front screen — paper only, snapshot numbers from the last app update; tap it to see its record. Nothing else changed or removed.
  • Superbrain and EdgeBoard are un-mixed — Superbrain screens show Superbrain numbers only. EdgeBoard keeps its own area and its own data, one tap away.
  • The Market Board now mirrors Kalshi's board — Kalshi's own strike and Yes/No prices come first, labeled Kalshi. When Kalshi blocks this phone, the row falls back to the Coinbase line and says so — it never fakes a Kalshi price. The board auto-syncs while the app runs and re-syncs fresh every new day.
  • Betting links into EdgeBoard — the Betting row under the board (and the button on the Betting Desk) takes you straight into the EdgeBoard area.
  • Signals live on the front screen — strike crosses, regime changes, distance building and window-open setups, generated by the app itself from its own reads while it's open and running.
  • Every decision now says UP or DOWN — "PLACE — DOWN (No) · pay 65¢ or less", "DON'T PLACE — leans DOWN" — on the front card, the board rows and the Trade Screen.
  • The app runs entirely on its own — nothing it does at run time calls Muse, Claude or any builder/AI service; only its usual public price feeds.

Reference — how it works
How it works & what the colors mean
How it works
Read the 15-minute markets • One best decision • You place the trade
1) Open 15-Min Targets — BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP are read live against each 15-minute window's line: spot vs the line, the distance, the clock and momentum.
2) The Trade Screen turns that read into one BEST DECISION — PLACE with the side and the price to pay, or DON'T PLACE with the reason. The front screen carries the same call, with a Market Board for all four coins.
3) Placed a trade in Kalshi yourself? Arm Trade Watch on it and the app warns you about sudden moves, flips and price swings while it stays open on screen — and mirrors your call on paper so the Win Rate screen can score it.
What the colors mean
GREEN = a PLACE read, or your side winning right now.
BLUE button = opens a screen or runs a check — it never spends anything.
AMBER = a warning — a sudden move, a flip, or a coin hugging the line.

Objective: every day find 3 Polymarket markets in Sports / Politics / Crypto where the price looks wrong vs the evidence, and give you a ticket for each.
The desk never places a real order. It prepares trade tickets — you approve them. Ticket slots stay blank until filled from real checked data: no markets, prices, probabilities or edges are invented here.
The desk team — lead + five specialists (reference)
The Desk — Lead + Five Specialists
Desk Lead
Runs the desk, assigns the work, and hands you the finished tickets. Nothing reaches you without passing Quant and the Risk Officer.
Scout
Scans markets closing in the next 7 days with over $50K volume. Flags 10c+ moves in 24h and markets where the news changed but the price didn't.
Researcher
Reads the market rules first: resolution source, deadline, edge cases. Then pulls the latest news and stats — and writes its own probability BEFORE looking at the price.
Quant
Edge = your probability − the market price. Passes only markets with 8c+ edge. Sizes with quarter Kelly, capped at your max stake.
Risk Officer
Enforces the hard limits below on every ticket. Any breach = reject — no exceptions, no overrides inside the desk.
Reviewer
Every night: scores closed tickets, what we got right and wrong, and brings you one rule change to approve. Keeps the log with win rate and ROI vs holding cash.
Risk Officer — Hard Limits
Max 5% of bankroll per trade
Max 15% open in one category
Nothing closing in under 2 hours
No averaging down
Any breach = reject
INTAKE FIRST — NO TRADE IDEAS YET
The desk's start rule: answer the 4 intake questions below first. No trade ideas or tickets are presented until you answer.

God Mode Parlay Builder — Kalshi 15-Min Legs Only
God Mode Parlay BuilderPAPER · GATE-PASSERS ONLY
The $1 Parlay Bot, rebuilt to the God Mode standard. A Kalshi 15-minute leg gets on a ticket ONLY when all four hold: the model's calibrated confidence is 60%+, the value vs the live Kalshi ask is positive, the ask actually loaded (never the Coinbase fallback line), and the ask is 85¢ or less. Tickets are same-window combos of 2–4 passing legs, ranked by the correlation-adjusted joint chance — the same joint math as Kalshi Lab combos. The app places nothing — copy the slip and place the legs yourself in Kalshi or Gambly. Lock a ticket and it is kept as a paper record and graded when the window settles.

Ticket Log — Saved on This Device

Best Sports Combos — Paper Only
Combos BuilderPAPER · MATH ONLY
Builds every 2-, 3- and 4-leg combo from the Sports tickets in your log above — plus 5-leg combos when fewer than 15 legs are available — and ranks them best first by expected value. For each combo: every leg, the combined price and payout per $1, the honest joint chance (your researched chances for the legs multiplied together — no boost, no hype) and the expected value. One losing leg loses the whole combo. Paper tickets only — the desk never places a real order. Same guardrails: stake is quarter Kelly, never more than 5% of bankroll per combo ticket (and never above your intake max stake), and combo stakes count toward the 15% Sports limit.

Desk Settings DESK BOOK ONLY
These settings run the new pipeline for NEW desk trades. The old Desk Stop % and Desk Target % controls are gone — new trades use the Risk stage's exits, fixed before entry. Imported Grok trades keep the stops and targets recorded on their cards.
Analyst floor: 70 — a coin scoring under 70 is skipped, no exceptions.
Sizer cap: 50% of current desk equity — size scales with the score (score 70 → 35% of equity, score 100 → 50%).
Exits, fixed at entry: hard stop −15% on every new desk position, no exceptions · at +60% sell half and move the stop on the rest to breakeven · trail the rest 25% from the peak · 45-minute max hold.
Day halt: if the desk's day P&L hits −15% of the day's starting equity, the desk stops until you restart it. Big-trade gate: any single trade over $25 needs your yes first.
Add a coin to the desk by hand
A hand add uses the same Sizer and Guard rules: the size comes from the coin's Analyst score (a coin the stream hasn't scored yet is sized at the floor score, 70). By hand: type the symbol, paste the coin's address, and type its current market size in SOL — the desk opens at that price.

The Grok routines — setup spec (reference)
The Grok Routines — the setup spec
R2 · Virtual $10 Desk scan ON
Schedule: every 30 minutes, weekdays 8:00 AM–6:30 PM ET.
Load current paper ledger at /cursor/stores/store-1ce963ad-280d-4040-b4f2-2152e303c290/virtual-10-desk/ledger.json. If missing, treat cash as $10 with no open positions. First, mark open positions to live prices. Honor hard stops (-8% to -15%) and trailing stops: if stop hit, close, update ledger, post exit with token, exit price, size, P&L, reason. As soon as position is green, move stop to breakeven. Once winner up 20%+, arm/ratchet trailing stop. Never place real trade/deposit/withdrawal. Then scan pump.fun, Solana, Base for launches/high-volume movers. Live data only; never invent. Open new paper trade only if: fewer than 3 open, size at most 30% equity, dollar risk to stop at most 10% equity, hard stop -8% to -15%, liquidity sufficient, clear reason. Post every new paper trade copyable: token name, contract, entry, size $, hard stop, target, short reason, plus DexScreener/pump.fun link. Update ledger, include brief running P&L (cash, open P&L, equity vs $10 start). If nothing worth trading and no exit/stop update, stay quiet.
R3 · Virtual $10 Desk end-of-day ON
Schedule: weekdays around 8:00 PM ET.
Deliver end-of-day paper summary for America/New_York day. Load ledger, mark open positions to live prices. Compute today's P&L, total P&L vs $10 start, cash, equity, open positions (entry, current, stop, target, unrealized P&L), and day's closed trades. Paper/sim only; never real trade/deposit/withdrawal. Send concise EOD summary in this chat, even if no trades: starting equity, current equity, today's P&L, open risk. Always send, including flat days.

You place the trade in Kalshi yourself. This only watches the round and alerts you — it does not know your real fill; your entry is what you type here.
Alerts only work while this app is open on screen — a closed app or locked phone watches nothing.
The app only knows about a trade when you arm it here — arm it right after you buy in Kalshi. The app places no Kalshi trades: real trades stay your taps in Kalshi. When you arm, the app also books the same side in its own 15-Min paper book (10% of its virtual balance, at your entry) — that mirror is paper only.
One watch per coin — arming the same coin again replaces it. It watches the round you arm it in and settles itself when that round ends. Alerts: crossed against you · losing ground (lead under half of what it was when you armed) · price drop (Kalshi bid 15¢+ under your entry — only when Kalshi loads) · 3 minutes left · round over.
Early warnings — what counts as “sudden” (fixed): SUDDEN MOVE = one price check moves against you by at least BTC $75 · ETH $2.50 · SOL $0.15 · XRP $0.0025 (once per round per direction; re-arms after 3 calm checks). MOVING FAST = still on your side, but at its speed over the last 3 checks it would reach the line within about 45 seconds (once per round; re-arms after the move dies out for 3 checks). PRICE SWING = your side’s Kalshi bid moves 10¢ or more between two checks (once per round; only when Kalshi really loaded — never faked).

Flip AlertsIN-APP ONLY
When a coin's live spot crosses to the other side of this round's target mid-round, an alert lands here and as a pop-up message — naming the coin, the target and which way it flipped. Works only while this tab is open and the phone is awake. A tiny wobble right on the line does not count: spot has to clear the target by a small band (BTC $10 · ETH $0.30 · SOL $0.016 · XRP $0.0003).

Round Record · Virtual $1 Balance · Self-LearningPAPER ONLY
Every 15-minute round the app reads is recorded: the target, the call it made (or NO PLAY), and how the round settled. The win rate is the real number from that record. Paper balance only — it never touches real money.
Reading the round record…
Session — Profit Vault & Cooldown—
Session discipline, worked off your tracked Kalshi balance and the app's own round record: the vault floor starts at 70% of the day's start and ratchets up to lock in half of any peak gain. Touch the floor and the session halts — no plays, no ticket or combo locks, no round-call locks — until you start a new session or a new day begins. Two straight losing round calls trigger a 15-minute cooldown. Predictions keep locking through both — measurement never stops.
Reading the session…
Late Session — 11 PM–12 AM ET—
Your late-session discipline, on paper in the app: the window is 11:00 PM–12:00 AM ET, BTC/ETH only. One settled loss in the window ends the day; ending the hour under your start triggers a 3-day break; $100 is the target. The app places nothing — your real trades stay your taps in Kalshi. Rounds the app locks in this hour stake 20% of its paper book; the rest of the day stakes 10%.
Reading the late session…

Entry Read: Analysis only, from this tab's own live prices. It flags when the entry picture changes — the entry itself is always your tap, in Kalshi.
If a price can't load, the card says so — after a 20-second settle window once the tab or app opens, and never while a refresh is still loading, so the opening refresh gets its chance first. A kept value is then tagged "stale" with the time it was last seen.
Win Rate: every Superbrain book's real record on one screen — the app's calls, your calls, your watched trades and the $10 Desk. Superbrain numbers only: EdgeBoard keeps its own record in its own area. Read only: nothing here books, changes or settles anything.
Reading your saved records…
Kalshi Lab: the app cannot read Kalshi's private code — it learns their patterns from real windows it observes: where Kalshi sets the strike vs the exchange open, and how Kalshi prices contracts vs the app's own model at the same distance and time. Every learned figure shows its sample count; under 30 samples it is labeled still learning. Display only — the app never places a trade, and no figure here is a profit promise.

GOD MODE—
No God Mode plays right now — the gate is strict on purpose.
Scan status — per sport
Edges: every pre-game moneyline side, checked against the gate. A pick passes only with EV of +5% or more, true chance of 55% or more and zero verify flags. Numbers are rounded down, never up.
Lines: verified game lines from a named sportsbook in ESPN's free feed — moneyline, spread and total. Lines only; the edge math lives in Edges.
Props: real player-prop markets from Kalshi's public, keyless feed, grouped by sport. Prices only — no verified true chance exists for these markets, so there is no EV and no gate badge here. A sport with no verified prop feed says so plainly.
Alerts: in-app only (a toast, the banner above, and this log). Fires when a pick newly passes the gate, or when a parlay leg's price moves or its game starts.
Parlay sync: a paper slip that re-prices every leg from the latest lines on each scan, and flags any leg whose price moved, whose game started, or whose line went stale. Paper only.
Paper bets: picks that passed the gate and that you chose to track. Settled from ESPN final scores. Fake money — nothing is ever placed.
Slip Parser: paste a pick — an X post, a Discord callout or a slip you typed. The app reads it right here on your phone with plain text rules (no AI service, no key), shows the legs for you to confirm or fix, and only then checks each leg against EdgeBoard’s verified lines. Paper only — nothing is ever placed.
Screenshots: not offered. Reading a picture needs an outside AI service and an API key, and this app uses neither — paste the text instead. Line shopping: EdgeBoard’s free feed carries one sportsbook per game, so legs are checked against that verified line, not shopped across books.
Parlay Bot: scans every league EdgeBoard covers, takes only picks that pass the gate (EV +5% or more, true chance 55% or more, zero flags — never loosened), and adds the highest-graded legs (at or above its learned minimum grade) until $1 pays at least $1,000. One paper slip. It never places a bet, and a $1-to-$1,000 slip is a long shot — the numbers below say exactly how long.
